title: AstraForge x Redwood - hybrid deployment & partnership framing
summary: Introductory partner discovery for hybrid GPU onramp. Discussed AstraForge's multi-region edge + cloud strategy, isolation requirements, expected throughput for inference workloads, pilot scope (3 months), and security/compliance checklist. Agreed to run a joint benchmark against a 4K token LLM path and validate VPC Peering + KMS flow.
topics: AstraForge infra: multi-region edge nodes + public cloud burst
Redwood deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Performance: batching, KV cache, quantization, latency SLOs
Pilot framing: success metrics, timeline, benchmark plan
action_items: Priya Desai: Share partner integration one-pager + high-level pricing ranges (due 2025-10-10)
Marco Alvarez: Draft benchmark plan for 4K token trace and share infra spec (due 2025-10-13)
Oliver Hayes: Provide sample traffic profile and list of top 5 prompt sets (due 2025-10-12)
next_steps: Exchange SOC2 and SAML integration docs via secure link
Kick off 3-month pilot after benchmark alignment
header:
Date: 2025-10-08 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 mins
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Oliver Hayes (AstraForge), Rina Kapoor (AstraForge), Samir Patel (AstraForge CTO)
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Desai: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin?
[00:06] Oliver Hayes: Oliver here - head of cloud partnerships at AstraForge. excited to chat re: hybrid onramp.
[00:10] Rina Kapoor: Rina, infra lead. we manage edge nodes and cloud bursting.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, CTO. i'll be listening for security and perf details.
[00:18] Marco Alvarez: Marco, solutions engineer at Redwood. i'll run through the technical parts.
[00:21] Priya Desai: goal for today is to understand AstraForge constraints, where Redwood fits — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and sketch a pilot.
[00:31] Oliver Hayes: sure, high level: we run regional edge racks in eu-west, us-east, ap-south. primary use case is low-latency inference for enterprise customers but with burst to public cloud for heavy batches. data residency and tenant isolation are big — some customers need physical separation.
[00:47] Rina Kapoor: additionally, some of our regulated customers require customer-managed KMS and audit trails. so any onramp needs to allow key control or HSM integration.
[00:56] Marco Alvarez: got it. Redwood supports three modes: hosted (fastest), dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC or on-prem). for KMS you can either use Redwood-managed KMS for hosted or configure KMS passthrough for private deployments. passthrough uses customer KMS + HSM where needed.
[01:16] Samir Patel: when you say passthrough, is that direct HSM call from the inference node or proxied via your control plane?
[01:22] Marco Alvarez: currently its proxied in our private deployment option — control plane still coordinates keys but we can enable an HSM connector that never stores plaintext in our plane. for dedicated the KMS contract is flexible; we can do envelope encryption with customer keys.
[01:36] Oliver Hayes: okay, security looks promising. on perf: our workloads are often 2k-6k token sequences — chat and long-form generation. we care about latency tail at p95 under 200ms for short queries and sub-second for longer streams. cost is important; we need a balance.
[01:57] Priya Desai: quick clarification — when you say 2k-6k tokens, is that the typical prompt length or response included?
[02:02] Oliver Hayes: combined — prompt plus expected response, say 3.5k average.
[02:06] Marco Alvarez: good to know. that informs batching and KV cache sizing. Redwood runtime has continuous batching and prefix KV caching; for long contexts we recommend KV caching + quantized model variants for cost.
[02:20] Rina Kapoor: quantization — do you have recommended profiles? we're worried about quality regressions.
[02:26] Marco Alvarez: yes, we ship recommended quantization profiles per model and workload. for e.g., 4-bit quant for long-context decoder models often keeps quality within a few percent depending on task. we also do model A/B via rollouts to validate.
[02:40] Samir Patel: are those rollouts automated? can you do canary and automatic fallback if quality drops?
[02:45] Marco Alvarez: yep — canary deploys, percentage rollouts, and automatic fallback to full-precision variant if evals detect regression on our prompt set.
[02:52] Oliver Hayes: intelligence here is good. one caveat: certain customers need on-prem or air-gapped options; will Redwood support complete offline private installs?
[03:02] Marco Alvarez: we have a private deployment package that can be deployed into a customer's VPC or on-prem. air-gapped is possible but requires a different workflow for model onboarding and patching; our team supports that as an enterprise engagement.
[03:13] Priya Desai: lets talk numbers — rough throughput and GPU sizing. what is your per-GPU expected rps for a 2k token seq?
[03:21] Marco Alvarez: depends on model. for a mid-size open model (approx 13B) on an A10-class GPU you might see ~6-8 rps for 2k tokens with batching. with 8-bit or 4-bit quant that improves. for longer 4k sequences throughput drops and memory pressure increases. we usually benchmark with your traces.
[03:37] Oliver Hayes: we can provide traces. our edge racks have A100-like capacity but some nodes are lower spec for cost reasons. we need routing policy so hot traffic hits low-latency instances and background batch jobs go to cheaper nodes.
[03:53] Marco Alvarez: smart routing is in our platform — policy-based routing by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or different regions if capacity constrained.
[04:05] Rina Kapoor: network — how do you handle KV cache across nodes? do you replicate or is cache local?
[04:10] Marco Alvarez: KV cache is local to the serving instance; we have prefix caching to minimize recompute. for multi-region you can seed caches during warmup. cross-node replication for KV isn't default; it adds latency.
[04:22] Oliver Hayes: hmm, that may affect our routing. we might need sticky routing for sessions to maintain low-latency for chat.
[04:29] Marco Alvarez: session stickiness is supported. you can pin sessions to pools or nodes.
[04:33] Samir Patel: security checklist — SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2 compliance, and per-tenant data retention controls. do you auto-purge data?
[04:44] Marco Alvarez: we support SAML, OIDC, role-based access, and long-form audit logs. data retention policies are configurable; private deploys give you full control. hosted customers can opt into retention windows and export logs. SOC2 reports are available under NDA.
[04:58] Rina Kapoor: encryption in transit? and egress controls?
[05:02] Marco Alvarez: TLS everywhere, mTLS for service-to-service. egress controls through VPC firewall rules in private deployments.
[05:09] Oliver Hayes: vendor lock-in risk — if we start with Redwood dedicated, can we export model artifacts and configs to our own infra later?
[05:18] Marco Alvarez: yes — we support model versioning and exportable configs. model binaries are standard formats; the runtime bindings are documented. some optimizations (our kernel selection) are runtime-specific but we try to keep formats portable.
[05:30] Priya Desai: let's surface pilot scope — suggested: 3 months, test traffic on us-east edge + cloud burst, benchmark base model and quant variant on 4k traces, validate KMS passthrough, and measure p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:47] Oliver Hayes: that aligns. success criteria: p95 latency under 500ms for long sequences, cost per 1k tokens below our current by at least 20%, and KMS integration without key export.
[05:59] Samir Patel: and compliance: SOC2 report review and SAML integration test are blockers before production.
[06:06] Marco Alvarez: understood. we'll include SOC2 docs and SAML integration checklist in the next packet.
[06:11] Rina Kapoor: about routing, we also want autoscale policies that prefer local edge until CPU/GPU saturated then burst to cloud — can Redwood autoscale cross-regions?
[06:21] Marco Alvarez: yes, autoscaling policies can be region-aware and policy-driven. you can configure thresholds and max burst to public clouds.
[06:28] Oliver Hayes: competitor note — we evaluated CloudChip; their performance graphing was weaker and no KV cache. Qubex AI offered better pricing but limited VPC features. interested in objective benchmark.
[06:41] Priya Desai: we'll run a neutral benchmark plan. Marco can propose metrics and scripts.
[06:46] Marco Alvarez: i'll propose a plan: 1) run 4k trace replay against a chosen model family in hosted sandbox, 2) run same trace against dedicated/private pilot nodes to measure diff, 3) capture p50/p95/p99, memory footprint, kernel timings, and token cost. aim to share results within two weeks of data receipt.
[07:05] Oliver Hayes: timeline wise, if we get the benchmark by mid-Oct, we can spin up pilot early Nov. procurement is typically 3-4 weeks after pilot signoff.
[07:16] Priya Desai: ok noted. any blockers from your side to provide traces?
[07:20] Oliver Hayes: we need an NDA for traces — contains customer prompts.
[07:23] Priya Desai: can do; i'll send an NDA and the secure upload link.
[07:27] Rina Kapoor: small technical Q: does Redwood's runtime require a specific container runtime on-prem? we use containerd 1.8 in our edge images.
[07:34] Marco Alvarez: we generally support Docker and containerd; for air-gapped installs we deliver OCI images and a deployment manifest compatible with k8s and containerd.
[07:44] Samir Patel: patch cadence — if we run private, how are security patches applied?
[07:48] Marco Alvarez: enterprise customers can choose automated patching via a control-plane connection or an offline patch bundle we provide. for air-gapped you must apply bundles manually.
[07:58] Oliver Hayes: ok. one more: telemetry — what observability do we expose for per-tenant cost/latency?
[08:04] Marco Alvarez: the Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, latency histograms, and trace-level sampling hooks. we can also stream logs to your SIEM.
[08:17] Rina Kapoor: good. any estimation on unit cost improvement from quantization + batching? ballpark?
[08:23] Marco Alvarez: rough ballpark: 30-60% reduction depending on profile; longer contexts benefit more from KV caching which can drop compute by 20-40% for repeated prefixes. exact numbers depend on model/seq distribution.
[08:37] Oliver Hayes: sounds reasonable. for pilot we want to compare 0/4-bit quant + baseline to see quality impact.
[08:44] Marco Alvarez: we'll include quality gates in the benchmark — BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics for generative tasks plus human evals on a small prompt set.
[08:55] Priya Desai: ok let's capture next steps and owners. Marco — benchmark plan and infra spec. Priya — NDA + partner one-pager. Oliver — traces and traffic profile.
[09:05] Oliver Hayes: yep. one administrative question — pricing cadence, are there reserved commitments for dedicated?
[09:11] Priya Desai: Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual commits; we can propose flexible burst credits for pilot. pricing ranges in the one-pager.
[09:20] Samir Patel: procurement note — we'll need contract language for data residency, indemnity, and termination; legal will want standard enterprise terms.
[09:29] Priya Desai: understood — we'll route that to our partnerships legal and share redlines.
[09:33] Marco Alvarez: any final technical clarifications?
[09:36] Rina Kapoor: nothing else from infra.
[09:38] Oliver Hayes: all good. thanks folks.
[09:40] Priya Desai: awesome. recap: NDA + upload link from Priya, benchmark plan from Marco, traces from Oliver. next meeting: technical deep-dive week of 10/20.
[09:52] Samir Patel: sounds good. thanks.
[09:55] Priya Desai: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "KV cache" appeared as "K V cash" in one line; "A100" got transcribed as "A-one-hundred" in a spot. Speakers overlapped briefly at 09:38 causing garbled phrase.
